critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
Real progress on the round-7 notes, but this is still not fern level. The best changes: the wide is now a native 1920 plate with a clean floor for the title. The scale has the depth of field it needed (focus 2.55 m, f/5.6). The post highlight on the scale dropped from 200-208 to about 172, below the display face (median about 188-190). The bag edges came up: the duffel's right end is about 42-59 depending on the sample and the case's right edge about 48, up from 18-27. In the shoulder, the hand lies flatter and no longer outshines the face. Hand and face now peak level (181 and 183, with the frame maximum on her face), and the hand's median (about 114-129) sits below the face's (about 141-149). Their p95s are about equal (about 165 against 162).

Four things still keep it amateur:
1. The new payment card does not read. It sits centred under the finger pads, so only a strip 6-8 px tall along its leading (agent-side) edge shows. The fingertips break that strip into three slivers that grade 100-139 on a cover of 85-93. The leading edge and the frame-left corner are there if you stretch the contrast, but at normal viewing the card reads as a lighter band on the passport, not a second object. Nothing in any of the four frames says 'pays'.
2. Dawn's face in the shoulder, the film's first face at 0:04, still has the stepped dark bands in the hair shell above the near ear and the pale knob on the frame-right jaw. Both were reported in round 7 and are unchanged: the head region differs from the round-7 frame by about 1 level on average.
3. In the profile, the agent's hands at the keys are the brightest skin (p95 about 200), well above either face (p95 about 155-170). Dawn's hand (p95 about 175) only matches her face's lit edge. The charcoal case also reads light grey there: its side is about 62-74 graded, against 35 in the scale and 36 in the wide, and the duffel beside it is about 51-63, against 26-33. In the round-7 profile, rendered before the light-linked 'scale bag edge' light existed, they were about 44 and 27. That light sits on the +X side, which is the side the profile camera (x 5.2) looks from.
4. The scale's opening frame is still about 40% near-black across its width (left counter-end slab median 14, right floor and wall 12). The composite's push to the readout is a 1.35x digital zoom (zoom [1.0, 1.35] in gfx/shots/scale_overweight.json), which takes the display from 178 to about 243 px. So the bags at the end of the push are upscaled from the 1920 plate.

The wide is the strongest frame and sits closest to pro. The shoulder close-up is where a viewer will judge the cast, and it is the weakest.
answers:
PINS AND EDGE (verified on the graded scale.jpg against scale.corners.json). I took each edge as the halfway point between the face (median about 188-190) and the bezel (15-27).
- Rows y 190/212/235: the left edge lies 1.7-1.9 px outside the left pins and the right edge 2.7-2.8 px outside the right pins.
- Columns x 1190/1260/1330: the top edge lies 1.9-2.2 px outside and the bottom edge 2.5-2.7 px outside.
- The 10-90% transition is 2-3 px.
Your 1.6-3.0 px and 2.1-2.7 px figures stand. The pins track the face, and the outward bias is the bleed hairline plus the residual defocus.
In scale_ow.png the face's own left edge rises 19 -> 52 -> 140 -> 181 -> 197 (10-90% in about 2-3 px). The letter strokes now ramp at about the same rate. Through the O (column x 1036) the top stroke falls 189 -> 176 -> 154 -> 114 -> 80 in about 3 px and rises again as fast. So each stroke edge is about 3 px, and the whole stroke is about 7-8 px across. tex_blur_px 1.25 has closed the round-7 blur note: the word sits on the glass at about the glass's own sharpness, and no further blur change is needed.

1) SCALE (0:00). It now works as an object shot. Duffel and case both sit on the plate with contact, the duffel's folds and straps read, and their frame-right edges separate from the dark. The display face is the brightest area (median about 188-190, max 198). The post's highlight now peaks at about 172 just under the head (207 in round 7), so the competition from the post is gone.
Two problems remain:
- Two small highlights still beat the face. The case's zip pullers (x 790-850, y 370-420) peak at 228, the frame's maximum, with about 57 px at or above the face median. The scale's back rim just right of the duffel (x 1080-1163, y about 803) peaks at 200, with about 43 px at or above it.
- The opening frame is about 40% near-black dead space across its width: the left counter end with its stepped shelf has a median of 14, the right floor and wall 12, and 59% of all pixels in the frame are below 20. The shelf reads as an abstract dark staircase.
In the composite, OVERWEIGHT reads at once on a desktop. The face is about 243 px wide, the word about 200 px wide and 34 px tall, and the type's darkest pixel is 30 on a face of about 178-190. But that size comes from a 1.35x digital push on the 1920 plate, so the duffel and case at the end of the push are upscaled. Natively the display is only 178 px wide (9% of the frame).

2) SHOULDER (0:04, 'she pays it'). Does the payment read immediately? No.
- The card sits centred under the pads (pose_cast: centre = pad + 5 mm in y - fwd*8 mm), so the hand covers most of it. What shows is a strip 6-8 px tall along its leading (agent-side) edge. The index and middle fingertips break it into three slivers about 26-30 px wide, graded 100-139 against a cover of 85-93. The leading edge and the frame-left corner (about x 432, y 614) are there, with a step of 30-50 levels to the cover, but the strip is too thin to read as an object.
- At 1280x720 it reads as a lighter band on the passport, not a second object. In the profile it is hidden under the hand, and in the wide it cannot be seen.
- The 'pays' beat is carried by the voice alone.
'Three finger pads meet the blank card within 0.3 mm': at pixel level the index, middle and ring pads touch the card with dark contact shadows and no visible gap, so I accept it. But contact is not the problem. Visibility is.
Other notes on this frame:
- The passport now shows its pale page edge (up to about 159) along the near side, a good gain.
- The hand still reads as a mannequin hand: three straight tube fingers, the pinky planted steeply on its tip, the thumb hidden.
- The counter ledge is still a plain grey slab (median about 63-80) across the bottom fifth. Apart from two soft queue posts in the background (q1_2 and q0_2, at about x 818 and 1005), nothing in frame says check-in. The frame reads as a desk, close to the inspection bench at 0:20.

3) WIDE (0:09, 2014 / CHINA). Is the floor clear for the title? Yes.
- In wide_2014.png the type box is x 144-350, y 797-953 ('2014' to x 350, 'CHINA' to x 322). Under it, with a 30 px margin, the plate has a median of 22, a p90 of 28, a p99 of 35 and a max of 36, with no post pixels.
- q1_0's base (projected at 221,733) ends about 60 px above the '20'.
- q1_1's base disc starts about 46 px right of the '4' and about 74 px right of 'CHINA'. Its shaft rises about 80 px right of the '4'.
- The date no longer looks planted on a post. q1_0 still stands directly above the '20' as a column over the date: acceptable, though moving it would help.
- The plate is native 1920, so the round-7 upscale note is closed.
Remaining nits:
- The near post q0_3 (1.0, -2.1) has its base disc reaching about y 1073-1077, 3-7 px from the frame bottom: a bright chrome form (dome up to about 170) almost cut at the bottom centre.
- The fire extinguisher at the left (x 100-125, y 520-600) is a faint maroon (chroma up to 12). The film reserves red for the seam.

4) BAGS ACROSS ANGLES.
- Scale and wide match: case 35/36, duffel 26/33, the duffel in front with the case behind and the display at the back corner.
- The profile breaks it. The case's side reads about 62-74, against the duffel's 51-63: a light grey nylon case instead of charcoal. The very likely cause is the 'scale bag edge' light at (SX+0.99, 0.42, PLATE+0.10), which is new this round and light-linked to both bags. It sits on the +X side, which is the side the profile camera (x 5.2) looks from, so it front-lights them for that camera. In the round-7 profile, rendered before that light existed, the case side was about 44 and the duffel about 27. The same light also lifts the case in the wide (about 25 before, 36 now), and that lift is what makes the wide match the scale.

5) PROFILE.
- The layout reads: Dawn at the ledge with her hand on the passport, the agent typing, the monitor between them and the bags on the scale below. The monitor now sits at about 149-152, an improvement.
- The agent's hands are the brightest skin. At the keys they reach a p95 of about 200, against about 155-170 for either face. Dawn's hand on the passport (p95 about 175) is about level with her face's lit edge, and the passport stack under it is edge-lit to about 220. Both faces have low medians (Dawn's about 63-80, the agent's about 65-108, depending on the mask) because most of each head is in shadow. The eye goes to hands and paper, not people.
- The agent's hands are less blue than his face and screen (b-r about 16, against 20 and 24), so a whiter light than the monitor mainly lights them. The likeliest is the island soft key (108 W). Its rays to the keyboard cross the agent flag's plane (z 2.35) at y 0.15-0.53, just in front of the flag's front edge at 0.55.
- The frame's maximum, 225, is a glint on the desk end's steel side reveal at (612, 446).
- The scale's display head and post are a dark vertical in the right fifth, running from the head (y about 345) to the bottom edge.
- On the right, the belt's two steel side rails (belt0_rail, top z 0.45) project as two faint horizontal lines at y about 520-535 and 595-616 (33-57 graded), which read as steps.
- A far-glazing mullion (projected x about 497) runs into the back of Dawn's crown and bun (head spans about x 481-555).

6) CAST ACROSS ALL FOUR ANGLES.
- Continuity holds: one Dawn, one agent, the same outfit, bun and flats, and the axis is kept (Dawn screen-left, agent screen-right in shoulder, profile and wide). Feet are grounded in the wide and the profile.
- In the shoulder close-up, the hair bands above the near ear and the knob on the frame-right jaw (x about 478-495, y 195-228, it reads as a pearl earring) are unchanged since round 7.
- The blank statue eyes read as closed lids at this size. That is acceptable by design, but it leaves the hand to carry the beat, and the hand reads as a mannequin's.
- The agent in the shoulder is a large, nearly unlit black mass over the right 20% of the frame (head median about 10, p95 about 49, against a background of about 17). That is fine for a dirty single, but he has no real rim to separate him from the dark background.

fixes.problem: The payment card sits centred under the finger pads, so only a strip 6-8 px tall along its leading edge shows. The fingertips break it into three slivers (100-139 on a cover of 85-93), so 'she pays it' does not read in any frame.
fixes.fix:
In pose_cast, move the card out past the fingertips toward the camera (the agent side). Replace centre = hand['pad'] + Vector((0, 0.005, 0)) - fwd * 0.008 with centre = hand['pad'] + fwd * 0.048 (fwd is already normalised). The card's centre then sits about 48 mm ahead of the pads. Its trailing edge stays under the fingertips, and its leading part overhangs the passport's agent-side edge by roughly 15-20 mm, casting a visible shadow line on the cover and the ledge.

Leave card.location.z as it is: desk() already sets it on top of the front cover, and the SOLIDIFY modifier (offset 1.0) builds its 0.76 mm upward. rest_hand's top_z (LEDGE + 0.04216) is the card's top surface. If the pads come off the card, drop top_z to LEDGE + 0.0414 so they rest on the cover instead of floating 0.76 mm above it.

Keep the card's slate material. It already grades 100-139, 15-50 levels above the cover, with a step of 30-50 levels at its edge. A lighter albedo would push it above the face (median about 141). Skip a chip: this camera sees the ledge at about 16-17 degrees, so the card's short side is only about 18-20 px tall and a chip would be about 13 x 3 px.

Re-render the shoulder and check:
- at least 1,100 px of card visible at 1280x720 (about 60% of its projected area of about 1,850 px);
- the leading edge and both leading corners clear of the fingertips;
- the card's graded median 110-135, under the face median of about 141.

fixes.problem: The film's first face, at 0:04, still shows hard stepped dark bands in the hair shell above the near ear, and a pale knob on the frame-right jaw at mouth level (x about 478-495, y 195-228). Both were reported in round 7 and are unchanged.
fixes.fix:
Bands. First find the cause with one shoulder test render, with the hair's BUMP Strength in people._sculpt_hair set to 0.0 (it is 0.05 now).
- If the bands vanish, they come from the TEX_WAVE node (the 'combed undulation' of the docstring). Raise its Scale from 22 to about 40, cut Distortion from 4.0 to about 1.0, and keep Strength at 0.05.
- If they stay, they are in the shape. Add hair.modifiers.new('relax', 'SMOOTH') directly after 'hug' (factor 0.8, 15 repeats), and raise hair.modifiers['hug'].offset from 0.0005 to about 0.0025.

Knob. Project Dawn's head-region vertices through the shoulder camera with project(cam, p, 1280, 720), and list which objects (body, ear, hair, bun, eye) land in x 478-495, y 195-228.
- If it is the far ear lobe, move her gaze target so the solved head turn drops by about 4 deg, or hide the lobe under the hair shell.
- If it is the bun, sink it further into the skull: change the -0.024 y offset in _sculpt_hair to about -0.032.

_sculpt_hair is shared by the whole cast, so check at 3x zoom in the shoulder and in one other stage that uses people.dawn().

fixes.problem: The charcoal case reads light grey in the profile: its side is about 62-74 graded, against 35 in the scale and 36 in the wide, and the duffel beside it is about 51-63, against 26-33. In the round-7 profile, before the 'scale bag edge' light existed, they were about 44 and 27. That light, at (SX+0.99, 0.42, PLATE+0.10), sits on the +X side, which is the side the profile camera (x 5.2) looks from, so it front-lights both bags for that camera.
fixes.fix:
Turn 'scale bag edge' off for the profile only. In build()'s render() wrapper, before calling orig, set bpy.data.objects['scale bag edge'].hide_render = (name == 'profile'), and set it back to False in the finally block. Do not turn it off for every camera except the scale: it also lifts the case in the wide (about 25 before, 36 now), and that lift is what makes the wide match the scale.

If the profile then needs separation on the bags, add a weak camera-invisible 3 W rim from behind the scale, at about (SX+0.2, 1.3, PLATE+0.6). Aim it at the bags, light-link it to the same 'scale bag edge receivers' collection, and hide it in the scale render if it changes that shot.

Target in the profile: case side about 35-45 graded and duffel about 25-35, matching the scale and wide.

fixes.problem: The agent's hands at the keys are the brightest skin in the frame (p95 about 200), well above either face (p95 about 155-170). Dawn's hand (p95 about 175) only matches her face's lit edge. The eye goes to the hands and the passport before either person.
fixes.fix:
Find the source before cutting anything. The agent's hands are less blue than his face and screen (b-r about 16, against 20 and 24), so a whiter light than the monitor mainly lights them. The likeliest is the island soft key (pos0_island, 108 W). Its rays to the keyboard cross the agent flag's plane (z 2.35) at y 0.15-0.53, just in front of the flag's front edge (0.55), so the flag does not shade them. Confirm with one profile test render with the island off.
- If the hands drop, add a second unseen flag that casts shadow only: every visibility flag off except shadow, as on 'pos0_hand flag2'. Make it about 0.70 x 0.35 m at (0.12, 0.47, 1.90). Rays from the island to his hands cross z 1.9 at about x -0.22 to 0.46 and y 0.29 to 0.62, which the flag covers. Rays to his face cross z 1.9 at y 0.68 or more, and rays to Dawn and to her hand on the passport at y 0.27 or less, so the flag cuts the hands without touching either face. Check that it clears his head.
- Then, for his face, raise mon_light's target tgt from z 1.45 to about 1.62 and cut its spread from 92 to about 60, so the screen's cone sits on his face and collar.

Dawn: in the render wrapper, for name == 'profile' only, raise 'counter eye bounce' from 2.5 W to about 7 W. It sits on the agent's side of the counter and lights the front of her face, the edge this camera sees.

Target in the profile: every hand's p95 at or below its own face's p95, with the lit side of each face the brightest skin in frame.

fixes.problem:
Three problems.
- The opening frame is about 40% near-black dead space across its width (left counter-end slab median 14, right floor and wall 12).
- The OVERWEIGHT composite reaches its readable size only through a 1.35x digital push on the 1920 plate (display 178 -> about 243 px), so the bags at the end of the push are upscaled.
- Two small highlights beat the display face (median about 188): the case's zip pullers (peak 228) and the plate's back rim just right of the duffel (peak 200, x 1080-1163, y about 803).
fixes.fix:
Resolution, not lens. Keep the 46 mm framing and render the scale plate larger: set final_res=(2880, 1620) in CAMERAS['scale'] and re-export scale.corners.json. doc_composite sizes the push from the plate width (k = W / PW * zoom), so the 1.0-1.35 push then stays at or above native resolution all the way (2880 / 1920 = 1.5). In gfx/shots/scale_overweight.json, multiply start_center and end_offset by 1.5, since they are in plate pixels. Consider starting the push at about 1.1 to trim part of the dead slab and floor at the open.

A longer lens does not fit. The frame runs from the display head's top (y about 136) to the plate's front rim (y about 1037): about 900 px at 46 mm, which becomes about 1,076 px at 55 mm. Projected with project(), 55 mm aimed at (1.52, 0.46, 0.70) puts the plate's front rim at y about 1160 and its left corner off the left edge.

Pullers. The case is one Tripo material whose metal and roughness both come from a single metallicRoughness texture. Testing the Principled node's Metallic value cannot pick out the pullers, and multiplying Base Color would darken the whole case. Instead, for dawn-suitcase only:
- pass the socket that feeds the BSDF's Metallic through a Math MULTIPLY (about 0.4);
- feed Roughness through a Math MAXIMUM of the texture's roughness and metallic x 0.6, so only the metal parts roughen.

Back rim. rim_f and rim_b use m['steel'] (roughness 0.22-0.4), which many trims share. Give the scale's front and back rims their own copy at roughness about 0.45-0.55.

Targets: pullers and rim at 170 or less graded, and nothing outside the display face at or above its median.

fixes.problem: The frame reads as a desk, not a check-in counter. A plain grey ledge slab (median about 63-80) runs across the bottom fifth, and the only airport signifiers are two soft queue posts in the background. The hand reads as a mannequin's: three straight tube fingers, the pinky planted steeply on its tip, the thumb hidden.
fixes.fix:
Add a handheld card terminal on the ledge between her hand and the agent: body 0.075 x 0.155 x 0.035 m, bevel 0.006, dark plastic m['plastic'], at about (0.18, 0.20, LEDGE + 0.035).
- Projected with project(), that lands at about x 740, y 610 at 1280x720. It sits on the ledge right of the passport and left of the agent's shoulder, whose dark mass starts at about x 830-870 at that height.
- Do not use (DAWN[0] - 0.02, 0.30): it projects to about (371, 668), frame-left below the passport, and its 0.155 m depth would overhang the ledge's back edge (y 0.318).
- Turned to face Dawn, its screen faces away from this camera, so here it reads as a dark shape on the grey ledge.
- For the profile, give it a blank screen_mat face 0.050 x 0.038 m (strength about 1.2, nothing on it) and twelve blank key bumps (a 4 x 3 grid, 0.010 x 0.008 x 0.002 m, no print).
- Keep any spill light at or under 2 W, so nothing near her hand outshines her face.

Hand, passing branch of rest_hand:
- pinky: set bends['pinky'] = curl + 0 and spread['pinky'] = 2, so it lies flat beside the ring finger instead of standing on its tip;
- thumb: change joints['thumb'] from (10, 25, 5, -5) to about (5, 40, 5, -15), so the thumb opens out and its tip shows frame-left of the index along the card (check the spread's sign at 3x zoom);
- other fingers: change the -12/-5 joint values to -6/-2, so the fingers keep a slight natural flex instead of hyper-straight tubes.
Check at 3x zoom.

fixes.problem: On the right, the belt's two steel side rails (belt0_rail, top z 0.45) project as two faint horizontal lines at y about 520-535 and 595-616 (33-57 graded), which read as steps. A far-glazing mullion (projected x about 497) runs into the back of Dawn's crown and bun (head spans about x 481-555).
fixes.fix:
Rails. The 'service wall wash' is not their source: the rails are fully metallic (steel_y, metal 1.0), so they show only reflections, and the wash has visible_glossy off. The rails are also what says 'bag belt', so a faint line is acceptable. If they should drop, roughen steel_y from (0.34, 0.49) to about (0.5, 0.6). It is used only on the belt rails and the scale's side rims, so recheck the scale shot afterwards.

Mullion. Changing the aim cannot help: a pure rotation moves her head and the far mullion together, and projected, the gap stays at 31 px. Move the camera instead: loc from (5.2, -0.38, 1.52) to about (5.2, -0.50, 1.52), keeping the aim. Projected, the far mullions then shift about 34 px left relative to her head, to about x 462 and 574. That leaves about 19 px between each of them and her head (bun back x about 481, face front about 555). Verify a gap of at least 15 px on both sides at full resolution.
